dataset_metadata.name: ARES-MED Expanded Pre-Processed Clinical RAG Protocols
dataset_metadata.source: Original 8 Spaceflight Scenarios + 32 NASA Space Medicine CPGs (CPG-01 through CPG-32)
dataset_metadata.description: Self-contained clinical protocol chunks preserving Layer-1 deterministic equations alongside 32 autonomous Level I-V Clinical Practice Guidelines.

legacy_8_scenarios.title: Acute and Chronic Hypercapnia (CO2 Toxicity & ECLSS Scrubbing Degradation)

symptoms_by_severity.mild_2.8_to_3.5_mmHg: Mild-to-moderate frontal headache, facial flushing, incipient lethargy.
symptoms_by_severity.moderate_3.5_to_4.5_mmHg: Throbbing frontal headache requiring analgesics, chronic dry cough, blurred vision, cognitive slowing.
symptoms_by_severity.severe_above_4.5_mmHg: Severe fatigue, malaise, nausea, exertional dyspnea, 5th cranial (trigeminal) nerve dysesthesia (facial numbness).

checs_medications.drug: Ibuprofen 400-600 mg PO or Acetaminophen 325-650 mg PO
checs_medications.contraindication: STRICT CONTRAINDICATION: Do NOT administer opioids (Hydrocodone/Hydromorphone) — suppresses central respiratory drive and worsens CO2 retention.

autonomous_checklist: Relocate crewmember out of low-ventilation compartment (Crew Quarters / Glovebox) immediately.
Deploy portable inter-module ventilation fans and run ECLSS diagnostics on CDRA 4BMS zeolite / CAMRAS amine beds.
If ppCO2 > 5.0 mmHg or trigeminal symptoms: deploy 100% O2 via demand mask (RSP) and run i-STAT venous blood gas (MDP).
Administer Ibuprofen 400 mg PO or Acetaminophen 650 mg PO from CMP (avoid opioids).
Suspend 75% VO2max ARED exercise and shift crew diet toward higher fat (RQ -> 0.85) to cut metabolic CO2 production by 20%.

legacy_8_scenarios.title: Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-Ocular Syndrome (SANS)

symptoms_by_severity.early_fd21_to_60: Asymptomatic optic disc edema on OCT or progressive near-vision blurriness (holding displays at arm's length).
symptoms_by_severity.advanced_fd60_plus: Persistent near-acuity degradation, dull retro-orbital pressure (worsened by CO2), metamorphopsia (straight-line distortion), scotomas.

checs_medications.contraindication: Screen anterior chamber angle before mydriasis.

checs_medications.drug: Acetazolamide PO (for progressive Frisen Grade >= 1 optic disc edema)
checs_medications.contraindication: Monitor electrolytes on i-STAT and kidney stone risk.

autonomous_checklist: Perform OCT (quantify RNFL > 105 um), Optical Biometry (axial length), Tonometry, and PanOptic Fundoscopy (MDP).
Prescribe adjustable Space Anticipation Glasses calibrated to +0.75 to +1.50 D hyperopic shift.
Initiate nightly Lower Body Negative Pressure (LBNP) therapy (reduces CVP to 1.2 mmHg and choroidal area expansion by 74%).
Apply Venoconstrictive Thigh Cuffs (VTCs), clamp cabin ppCO2 < 2.5 mmHg, and moderate peak ARED Valsalva loads.

legacy_8_scenarios.title: Orthostatic Intolerance and Gravitational Transition Pre-Syncope

symptoms_by_severity.compensatory_1_to_3_min: Postural lightheadedness, dizziness, palpitations, weakness, mild visual blurring.
symptoms_by_severity.presyncope_4_to_6_min: Tunnel vision ('graying out'), diaphoresis, epigastric nausea, tinnitus, impending syncope.

checs_medications.drug: 0.9% Normal Saline 500-1000 mL IV + AstroAde / Salt Tablets PO
Ondansetron 4 mg ODT or Promethazine 25 mg IM/IV
checs_medications.contraindication: Promethazine may cause sedation; co-administer judiciously.

autonomous_checklist: Command crewmember into immediate supine, legs-elevated (Trendelenburg) posture to restore venous return.
Attach Inspiratory Threshold Valve (ITV / ITD) to facemask (RSP) — boosts stroke volume to 138 mL and cardiac output to 8.9 L/min.
Don lower-body compression garments and execute NASA Fluid Loading Protocol (1.0-1.5 L isotonic fluid).
If severe post-landing hypotension persists: infuse 500-1,000 mL 0.9% Normal Saline via CHeCS IV pump (ISP).

legacy_8_scenarios.title: Acute Radiation Syndrome (ARS) from Solar Particle Event (SPE)
nasa_citations: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 Rev C [V1 4030] Space Permissible Exposure Limits

symptoms_by_severity.prodromal_1_to_6_hr: Sudden anorexia, severe nausea, retching, repetitive vomiting, acute fatigue.
symptoms_by_severity.manifest_6_to_48_hr: Throbbing headache, parotid gland tenderness, watery diarrhea, cutaneous erythema.

checs_medications.drug: Ondansetron 4-8 mg ODT/IV, Levofloxacin 500 mg PO, Valacyclovir, Fluconazole, Acetaminophen
checs_medications.contraindication: STRICT CONTRAINDICATION: Avoid Aspirin and NSAIDs (Ibuprofen/Ketorolac) — radiation thrombocytopenia creates severe GI hemorrhage risk.

autonomous_checklist: ALARA Protocol: Abort EVA immediately upon DONKI /FLR or /SEP notification; retreat to high-hydrogen Storm Shelter.
Administer Ondansetron 4-8 mg ODT/IV (OMP/TIMP) and initiate 0.9% Normal Saline IV rehydration (ISP) with i-STAT electrolytes.
Perform serial C2M2 offline Complete Blood Count (CBC) assays every 6 hours to track Andrews lymphocyte depletion kinetics.
Initiate prophylactic antimicrobials (Levofloxacin, Valacyclovir, Fluconazole) and use Acetaminophen (NO NSAIDs/Aspirin) for fever.

legacy_8_scenarios.title: EVA Thermal Strain ('Space Fever'), Dehydration, and Decompression Sickness (DCS)

symptoms_by_severity.thermal_strain: Profuse cranial sweat pooling across eyes, visor fogging, intense heat discomfort, muscle cramps, cognitive disorientation.
symptoms_by_severity.dcs_type_I_and_II: Deep periarticular shoulder/knee pain ('the bends'), substernal burning chest pain, paroxysmal cough ('the chokes'), scotomas.

checs_medications.drug: 100% Oxygen (RSP) + 0.9% Normal Saline 1-2 L IV (ISP) + Ibuprofen 600 mg PO / Ketorolac 30 mg IV (TIMP)
checs_medications.contraindication: Rule out intracerebral hemorrhage before high-dose Ketorolac.

autonomous_checklist: Order immediate EVA work-rest pause (reduce VO2 < 1,000 mL/min) and set LCVG cooling water flow to maximum.
Abort EVA, ingress airlock, and repressurize to 101.3 kPa (14.7 psia) to compress nitrogen microbubbles.
Doff spacesuit and apply active surface cooling packs (neck, axillae, groin) until CBT < 38.0 °C.
Place astronaut on 100% O2 via tight-fitting mask (RSP), infuse 1.0-2.0 L Normal Saline IV (ISP), and run i-STAT panel.

legacy_8_scenarios.title: Circadian Desynchrony, Sleep Architecture Fragmentation, and Behavioral Asthenia
nasa_citations: NASA Spaceflight Standard Measures (SSM) — Sleep & Cognition Test Battery (CTB)

symptoms_by_severity.subacute_drift: Difficulty falling asleep, frequent awakenings, daytime cognitive fog, slowed visual reaction speed (+30% on CTB).
symptoms_by_severity.acute_behavioral: Irritability, declining motivation, acute anxiety or agitation crisis (>24 hours).

checs_medications.drug: Melatonin 3-5 mg PO, Zaleplon 5-10 mg PO (onset), or Zolpidem 5-10 mg PO (maintenance); Modafinil/Caffeine (daytime)
checs_medications.contraindication: If benzodiazepines (Lorazepam/Diazepam) are used for acute agitation, stage Flumazenil 0.1 mg/mL (EMTP) for reversal.

autonomous_checklist: Configure dynamic solid-state lighting: 480 nm blue-enriched light upon waking; blue-depleted dim light 2 hours pre-sleep.
Cool Crew Quarters to 18-20 °C ([V2 6012]) and verify local sleep-station fan & ppCO2 < 2.5 mmHg.
Administer Melatonin 3 mg PO or Zaleplon 5-10 mg PO at bedtime (OMP); use Caffeine/Modafinil prior to critical EVA/docking.
Activate C2M2 offline VR relaxation, CBT modules, and asynchronous Private Psychological Conference.

legacy_8_scenarios.title: Spaceflight Venous Thromboembolism (IJV Thrombosis) and Cardiac Arrhythmia

symptoms_by_severity.ijv_thrombosis: Unilateral neck fullness, dull ache along sternocleidomastoid/clavicle, unilateral facial congestion, headache.
symptoms_by_severity.pe_or_vt: Sudden pleuritic chest pain, acute resting dyspnea, palpitations, presyncopal dizziness.

checs_medications.drug: Enoxaparin SC -> Apixaban PO (Vascular Contingency Pack); Metoprolol, Nitroglycerin, Epinephrine (EMTP)
checs_medications.contraindication: HIGH TRAUMA BLEED RISK: Immediately restrict EVA and high-load ARED exercise; stage Protamine (for Enoxaparin) and PCC (for Apixaban).

autonomous_checklist: Perform C2M2 AI-guided neck ultrasound to confirm IJV thrombus and assess compressibility/Doppler flow.
Initiate subcutaneous Enoxaparin followed by oral Apixaban from the Vascular Contingency Pack (VCP).
Lock out crewmember from EVA and high-load ARED resistive exercise; stage Protamine and PCC reversal agents.
If VT/VF cardiac arrest occurs: secure crewmember to electrically isolated CMRS, defibrillate via AED/Zoll, place ILMA airway (RSP), and administer Epinephrine 0.1 mg/mL (EMTP).

legacy_8_scenarios.title: Early-Mission Space Adaptation Syndrome (SAS), Rhinosinusitis, and Acute Urinary Retention
nasa_citations: ISS Medical Checklist JSC-48522 (SAS & Bladder Catheterization)

symptoms_by_severity.sas_and_sinus: Severe motion-induced nausea/vomiting, pallor, 'space stuffies' nasal congestion, sinus headache, ear fullness.
symptoms_by_severity.urinary_retention: No void >8-12 hours (bladder volume >600 mL post-promethazine), suprapubic fullness, lower abdominal pain.

checs_medications.drug: Promethazine 25-50 mg PO/IM/IV + Caffeine 100-200 mg PO; Tamsulosin 0.4 mg PO; Lidocaine Jelly; Nitrofurantoin
checs_medications.pack: CMP, OMP, TIMP, Minor Treatment Pack (MTP)
checs_medications.contraindication: Anticholinergic antiemetics (Promethazine/Meclizine) precipitate urinary retention in microgravity — monitor bladder volume.

autonomous_checklist: For SAS: Minimize head pitch/roll movements; administer Ondansetron 4 mg ODT or Promethazine 25 mg + Caffeine 100-200 mg (CMP/TIMP).
For Cephalad Rhinosinusitis: Administer Pseudoephedrine PO and Oxymetazoline nasal spray (limit <= 3 days).
If unable to void >8 hours: Perform AI-guided bladder ultrasound (MDP) and administer Tamsulosin 0.4 mg PO (OMP).
If bladder volume >500 mL: Perform sterile urethral catheterization per JSC-48522 using Lidocaine Jelly and MTP catheter kit.

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Acute Appendicitis (Non-Operative Level V Management)
diagnostic_criteria: RLQ abdominal pain, anorexia, fever, rebound tenderness
C2M2 CBC: Leukocytosis with left shift
Ultrasound-2 RLQ scan: Non-compressible dilated appendix (>6 mm) / periappendiceal fluid
autonomous_checklist: Keep crewmember NPO (nothing by mouth) and initiate IV fluids via ISP
Verify C2M2 WBC and i-STAT Chem8+ / CG4+ lactate
Administer broad-spectrum IV carbapenem or cephalosporin (Ertapenem 1 g IV q24h or Ceftriaxone 1-2 g IV)
Provide IV analgesia (Hydromorphone 1-2 mg IV) if ppCO2 is nominal
drug_lockouts: Bisacodyl (acute surgical abdomen)
Ibuprofen / Ketorolac / Aspirin (bleeding/perforation risk)
clinical_practice_guidelines.search_text: CPG-01 Acute Appendicitis Level V non-operative RLQ pain leukocytosis C2M2 Ultrasound-2 Ertapenem Ceftriaxone Hydromorphone NPO IV fluids.

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) / Myocardial Infarction
diagnostic_criteria: Substernal chest pain, diaphoresis, dyspnea, radiating arm/jaw pain
Tempus Pro 12-lead ECG: ST-segment elevation/depression or T-wave inversion
autonomous_checklist: Place crewmember at rest with continuous Tempus Pro 12-lead ECG & SpO2
Administer Aspirin 325 mg PO (chewed) if no thrombocytopenia/hemorrhage
Administer Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL q5min x3 PRN only if SBP >= 90 mmHg and no PDE5i use
Initiate Clopidogrel 300 mg PO load -> 75 mg daily, Atorvastatin 40-80 mg PO, and Enoxaparin 1 mg/kg SQ
drug_lockouts: Nitroglycerin if SBP < 90 mmHg or PDE5 inhibitor use
Aspirin/Clopidogrel/Enoxaparin if ARS thrombocytopenia
clinical_practice_guidelines.search_text: CPG-02 Acute Coronary Syndrome ACS MI chest pain Tempus Pro 12-lead ECG Aspirin Nitroglycerin Clopidogrel Atorvastatin Enoxaparin.

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Cardiac Arrest / Ventricular Fibrillation (ACLS)
diagnostic_criteria: Unresponsive, apneic, pulseless
Tempus Pro ECG: Ventricular Fibrillation (VF), pulseless VT, PEA, or Asystole
autonomous_checklist: Secure crewmember and rescuer using microgravity Crew Medical Restraint System (CMRS)
Initiate high-quality chest compressions (handstand/reverse bear-hug technique in 0G)
Deliver unsynchronized biphasic defibrillation via Tempus Pro for VF/pVT
Administer Epinephrine 1 mg IV q3-5min via ISP access and monitor ETCO2
drug_lockouts: Ensure no conductive fluid/oxygen pooling before defibrillation shock
clinical_practice_guidelines.search_text: CPG-03 Cardiac Arrest ACLS VF pVT defibrillation Tempus Pro Epinephrine 1 mg IV CMRS microgravity CPR.

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Internal Jugular Vein (IJV) Thrombosis
diagnostic_criteria: Cephalad fluid shift, neck fullness/asymmetry, facial plethora
Ultrasound-2 Compression & Color Doppler: Grade 3/4 non-compressible occlusive or stagnant flow in IJV
autonomous_checklist: Confirm IJV occlusion grade via Ultrasound-2 Doppler
Verify baseline C2M2 platelets and absence of active trauma/bleeding
Initiate Enoxaparin 1 mg/kg SQ q12h bridge, then transition to Apixaban 10 mg PO BID x7d -> 5 mg PO BID
Stage Protamine Sulfate and Prothrombin Complex Concentrate (PCC) for emergency reversal
drug_lockouts: Active trauma, internal hemorrhage, planned surgery, severe thrombocytopenia
clinical_practice_guidelines.search_text: CPG-04 Internal Jugular Vein IJV Thrombosis Ultrasound-2 Grade 3 4 Doppler Enoxaparin Apixaban Protamine PCC.

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Supraventricular Tachycardia / Atrial Fibrillation
nasa_citations: ISS Holter & Tempus Pro Rhythm Protocol
diagnostic_criteria: Palpitations, lightheadedness, irregular or narrow-complex tachycardia (>130-150 bpm)
Tempus Pro / Holter 12-lead ECG: Afib or SVT; check QTc interval
autonomous_checklist: Run Tempus Pro 12-lead ECG and check i-STAT Chem8+ (K+, iCa)
If hemodynamically stable, perform vagal maneuvers (Valsalva) and administer Metoprolol 25-50 mg PO
If unstable (hypotension, chest pain, altered mental status), perform synchronized cardioversion
drug_lockouts: Caffeine, Modafinil
Metoprolol if cardiogenic shock, bradycardia, or imminent reentry G-transition
clinical_practice_guidelines.search_text: CPG-05 Supraventricular Tachycardia SVT Atrial Fibrillation Afib Tempus Pro Holter Metoprolol i-STAT K+.

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)
diagnostic_criteria: Hyperopic visual acuity shift, near-vision blurring, headache
Ultrasound-2: Optic Nerve Sheath Diameter (ONSD) > 5.9 mm
PanOptic / OCT: Optic disc edema (Frisen >= 1), choroidal folds, RNFL thickening, globe flattening
autonomous_checklist: Measure ONSD via Ultrasound-2 and perform OCT / PanOptic fundoscopy
Verify cabin ppCO2 < 2.0 mmHg (V2 6073) as hypercapnia exacerbates cerebral vasodilation
Apply Lower Body Negative Pressure (LBNP) / thigh cuffs to reverse cephalad fluid shift
Deploy spaceflight corrective lenses if hyperopic shift impairs operations
drug_lockouts: Pseudoephedrine (elevates IOP and blood pressure)
clinical_practice_guidelines.search_text: CPG-06 SANS Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome ONSD > 5.9 mm Ultrasound-2 OCT PanOptic Frisen choroidal folds RNFL ppCO2 LBNP.

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Acute Hypercapnia (Cabin CO2 Toxicity)
diagnostic_criteria: Cabin ppCO2 > 3.0 mmHg (1h avg) or > 2.5 mmHg (24h avg)
Throbbing frontal headache, tachypnea, dyspnea, cognitive slowing
Tempus Pro ETCO2 elevated; i-STAT CG4+ elevated pCO2 / respiratory acidosis
autonomous_checklist: Activate backup CO2 scrubber / LiOH canisters and increase module airflow ventilation
Monitor crewmember ETCO2 via Tempus Pro and blood gases via i-STAT CG4+
Administer Acetaminophen 325-650 mg PO for CO2-induced headache
drug_lockouts: Hydrocodone/APAP, Hydromorphone (opioid respiratory depression)
Zolpidem (CNS/respiratory depression)
clinical_practice_guidelines.search_text: CPG-07 Acute Hypercapnia CO2 toxicity V2 6073 ppCO2 > 3.0 mmHg headache ETCO2 i-STAT CG4+ lockout opioids Zolpidem.

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Decompression Sickness (DCS)
diagnostic_criteria: EVA suit pressure drop or rapid cabin depressurization (>0.5 kPa/min)
Deep joint pain ('bends'), paresthesias, cutis marmorata, vertigo, or neurological deficits
autonomous_checklist: Immediately administer 100% Oxygen via mask/suit
Initiate hyperbaric repressurization in airlock or suit (Bends Treatment Apparatus)
Administer aggressive IV/oral isotonic fluids (ISP) to support intravascular volume
Perform serial neurological exams and hold all non-emergent EVAs
drug_lockouts: Sedatives that mask neurological deterioration
clinical_practice_guidelines.search_text: CPG-08 Decompression Sickness DCS bends EVA suit pressure drop V2 6081 100% O2 hyperbaric repressurization IV fluids.

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Acute Radiation Syndrome (ARS) / Solar Particle Event (SPE)
diagnostic_criteria: SPE dosimetry alert; BFO dose > 250 mGy-Eq (30d) or career > 600 mSv
Prodromal nausea, vomiting, fatigue within hours of exposure
C2M2 CBC: Rapid Absolute Lymphocyte Count (ALC) drop and progressive thrombocytopenia
autonomous_checklist: Order immediate ingress to spacecraft solar storm shelter (ALARA, V1 4031)
Perform serial C2M2 CBC (ALC & platelets) every 6-12 hours for biological dosimetry
Administer Ondansetron 4-8 mg ODT for prodromal emesis and IV hydration (ISP)
Monitor for neutropenic fever and avoid IM injections if platelets drop
drug_lockouts: Aspirin, Ibuprofen, Ketorolac, Enoxaparin, Apixaban, Clopidogrel (thrombocytopenia hemorrhage)
Trimethoprim/SMX (bone marrow suppression)
Loperamide (if radiation GI syndrome)
clinical_practice_guidelines.search_text: CPG-09 Acute Radiation Syndrome ARS SPE Solar Particle Event V1 4030 Table 4.8-1 BFO 250 mGy-Eq C2M2 ALC thrombocytopenia Ondansetron.

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Ammonia (NH3) Toxic Inhalation / Coolant Leak
diagnostic_criteria: Cabin NH3 > 30 ppm (1-hour SMAC)
Severe ocular burning, lacrimation, cough, wheezing, laryngospasm
autonomous_checklist: Don portable breathing apparatus (PBA) / 100% O2 mask and isolate affected cooling loop
Perform continuous eye irrigation with sterile saline
Administer Albuterol 90 mcg inhaled (RSP) for bronchospasm; transition to Fluticasone/Salmeterol for recovery
drug_lockouts: Avoid topical ocular steroids if chemical corneal epithelial defect exists
clinical_practice_guidelines.search_text: CPG-10 Ammonia NH3 toxic inhalation coolant leak JSC 20584 SMAC 30 ppm 1h Albuterol Fluticasone Salmeterol eye irrigation.

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Hydrazine (N2H4) Propellant Exposure
diagnostic_criteria: Post-EVA suit propellant contamination; cabin N2H4 > 4 ppm (1-hour SMAC)
Airway irritation, bronchospasm, dizziness, hepatic injury, or seizures
autonomous_checklist: Isolate contaminated EVA suit in airlock and scrub cabin atmosphere
Administer Albuterol 90 mcg inhaled (RSP) and supplemental O2 for bronchospasm
Monitor hepatic/metabolic status on i-STAT Chem8+ / CG4+
drug_lockouts: Acetaminophen, Fluconazole, Atorvastatin if hydrazine-induced hepatotoxicity occurs
clinical_practice_guidelines.search_text: CPG-11 Hydrazine N2H4 propellant exposure post-EVA JSC 20584 SMAC 4 ppm 1h Albuterol hepatotoxicity.

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Carbon Monoxide (CO) / Spacecraft Fire Smoke Inhalation
diagnostic_criteria: Cabin fire/pyrolysis event; CO > 425 ppm (1-hour SMAC)
Headache, confusion, tachypnea, soot in airway (Note: standard SpO2 may read falsely normal)
autonomous_checklist: Don PBA / 100% high-flow O2 immediately to displace carboxyhemoglobin
Monitor i-STAT CG4+ lactate/acidosis and Tempus Pro ECG for ischemia
Administer Albuterol 90 mcg inhaled (RSP) for smoke-induced bronchospasm
drug_lockouts: Sedatives or opioids that depress ventilation
clinical_practice_guidelines.search_text: CPG-12 Carbon Monoxide CO spacecraft fire smoke inhalation JSC 20584 SMAC 425 ppm 1h 100% O2 Albuterol.

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Space Motion Sickness (SMS) / Space Adaptation Syndrome
diagnostic_criteria: First 24-72 hours of microgravity or G-transition
Nausea, vomiting, malaise, pallor, stomach awareness, vestibular disorientation
autonomous_checklist: Minimize rapid head pitch/roll movements during neuro-vestibular adaptation
If crewmember must remain operationally alert, administer Ondansetron 4-8 mg ODT
If sleep/rest window is available and refractory, use Promethazine 25-50 mg PO/IV or Meclizine 25 mg PO
drug_lockouts: Promethazine / Meclizine during EVA, docking, or robotics (severe sedation); avoid IM Promethazine if IV available
clinical_practice_guidelines.search_text: CPG-13 Space Motion Sickness SMS Space Adaptation Syndrome SAS nausea vomiting Ondansetron ODT Meclizine Promethazine.

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Orthostatic Intolerance (Post-Landing / G-Transition)
diagnostic_criteria: Reentry / landing or planetary surface gravity transition
SBP drop >= 20 mmHg, HR spike > 30 bpm, presyncope, tunnel vision
autonomous_checklist: Place crewmember supine / recumbent and inflate anti-G / compression garments
Administer oral salt + fluid loading or IV Normal Saline bolus (ISP)
Monitor continuous BP and ECG via Tempus Pro
prescribed_meds: IV Normal Saline / Electrolyte Fluid Load (ISP)
drug_lockouts: Metoprolol, Lisinopril, Nitroglycerin (worsen orthostatic collapse)
clinical_practice_guidelines.search_text: CPG-14 Orthostatic Intolerance post-landing reentry G-transition presyncope fluid loading compression garments lockout Metoprolol Lisinopril.

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: EVA Thermal Heat Strain / Hyperthermia
diagnostic_criteria: LCVG cooling failure or metabolic rate > 470 W during EVA
Core body temperature >= 38.5 C (caution) or >= 39.0 C (mandatory EVA abort), tachycardia, confusion
autonomous_checklist: Abort EVA immediately if core temp >= 39.0 C or neurological signs appear
Remove suit in airlock, apply active surface cooling, and measure i-STAT Chem8+ electrolytes
Rehydrate aggressively with chilled oral/IV fluids (ISP)
drug_lockouts: Caffeine, Modafinil, Pseudoephedrine (worsen tachycardia/dehydration)
clinical_practice_guidelines.search_text: CPG-15 EVA Thermal Heat Strain Hyperthermia V2 11032 LCVG failure core temp 38.5 39.0 C abort cooling hydration.

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Nephrolithiasis (Renal Colic / Kidney Stones)
diagnostic_criteria: Acute severe unilateral flank pain radiating to groin, hematuria, nausea
Ultrasound-2: Hydronephrosis or ureteral jet asymmetry
autonomous_checklist: Check i-STAT Chem8+ creatinine before administering parenteral NSAIDs
Administer Ketorolac 15-30 mg IV/IM (if creatinine normal) + Ondansetron 4-8 mg ODT
Initiate high-volume IV/oral hydration (ISP) and strain urine to capture stone
If refractory pain and normal ppCO2, titrate Hydromorphone 1-2 mg IV
drug_lockouts: Ketorolac / Ibuprofen if i-STAT creatinine elevated
Hydromorphone if hypercapnia present
clinical_practice_guidelines.search_text: CPG-16 Nephrolithiasis Renal Colic kidney stone flank pain Ultrasound-2 hydronephrosis Ketorolac i-STAT creatinine hydration.

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Urinary Retention (Microgravity Detrusor Stasis)
diagnostic_criteria: Inability to void, suprapubic fullness/pain
Ultrasound-2 Bladder Scan: Distended bladder (>400-500 mL)
autonomous_checklist: Confirm bladder distension via Ultrasound-2
Perform sterile intermittent straight or Foley catheterization
Screen medication list and discontinue anticholinergics/decongestants
drug_lockouts: Diphenhydramine, Pseudoephedrine, Hydrocodone, Hydromorphone (worsen urinary retention)
clinical_practice_guidelines.search_text: CPG-17 Urinary Retention microgravity detrusor stasis Ultrasound-2 bladder scan catheterization lockout Diphenhydramine Pseudoephedrine.

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Urinary Tract Infection (Cystitis & Pyelonephritis)
diagnostic_criteria: Dysuria, urgency, frequency (cystitis); flank pain, fever, C2M2 leukocytosis (pyelonephritis)
autonomous_checklist: For uncomplicated cystitis: Nitrofurantoin 100 mg PO BID x5-7d (monitor for failure if early-flight elevated GFR)
For pyelonephritis or systemic fever: Ceftriaxone 1-2 g IV q24h or Levofloxacin 500 mg PO q24h
Ensure high oral/IV hydration
drug_lockouts: Nitrofurantoin for pyelonephritis
Levofloxacin during heavy EVA/ARED loading (Achilles tendon rupture risk)
clinical_practice_guidelines.search_text: CPG-18 UTI Urinary Tract Infection cystitis pyelonephritis Nitrofurantoin Levofloxacin Ceftriaxone GFR Achilles tendon.

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Pneumonia & Systemic Sepsis
diagnostic_criteria: Fever, productive cough, tachypnea, SpO2 < 94%, hypotension
C2M2 CBC: Leukocytosis; i-STAT CG4+: Elevated lactate (>2.0 mmol/L)
autonomous_checklist: Check Tempus Pro 12-lead ECG (QTc) and i-STAT CG4+ lactate
Initiate Ceftriaxone 1-2 g IV q24h + Azithromycin 500 mg PO (if QTc <= 470 ms) OR Levofloxacin 500 mg PO
Resuscitate hypotension with IV crystalloids (ISP) and supplemental O2
prescribed_meds: Ertapenem (TIMP, 1 g IV if severe sepsis)
drug_lockouts: Azithromycin if QTc > 470 ms on Tempus Pro
Levofloxacin if heavy EVA/ARED
clinical_practice_guidelines.search_text: CPG-19 Pneumonia Sepsis fever hypoxia C2M2 leukocytosis i-STAT CG4+ lactate Ceftriaxone Azithromycin QTc Tempus Pro.

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Anaphylaxis / Severe Allergic Reaction
diagnostic_criteria: Acute urticaria, angioedema, stridor, wheezing, hypotension after allergen/drug exposure
autonomous_checklist: Administer Epinephrine 0.3 mg IM (lateral thigh) immediately
Establish IV access (ISP), administer IV Normal Saline bolus and supplemental O2
Administer Diphenhydramine 25-50 mg IV/IM and Albuterol 90 mcg inhaled for bronchospasm
Monitor continuously on Tempus Pro ECG and NIBP
drug_lockouts: No contraindication to Epinephrine in anaphylaxis
clinical_practice_guidelines.search_text: CPG-20 Anaphylaxis severe allergic reaction Epinephrine 0.3 mg IM Diphenhydramine Albuterol Tempus Pro.

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Regolith Dust Conjunctivitis & Airway Irritation
diagnostic_criteria: Post-EVA cabin dust exposure; ocular redness, itching, sneezing, mild wheezing
autonomous_checklist: Irrigate eyes with sterile saline; inspect with PanOptic fluorescein + cobalt filter to rule out corneal abrasion
If cornea intact: Olopatadine 0.2% ophthalmic drops + Carboxymethylcellulose 0.5% lubricant
Administer Fexofenadine 180 mg PO (non-sedating) and Albuterol 90 mcg inhaled if wheezing
drug_lockouts: Olopatadine if corneal abrasion detected
Diphenhydramine pre-EVA (sedation)

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Corneal Abrasion / Particulate Eye Trauma
diagnostic_criteria: Acute foreign-body eye pain, photophobia, tearing
PanOptic Fundoscope (Cobalt blue filter): Fluorescein uptake defect on cornea
autonomous_checklist: Flush eye gently with sterile saline to clear particulate
Perform fluorescein exam via PanOptic to confirm epithelial defect
Apply Mineral Oil / Petrolatum ophthalmic ointment for nocturnal protection and give Acetaminophen PO
drug_lockouts: Olopatadine, topical corticosteroid eye drops (impair corneal healing)

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Odontogenic Abscess & Barodontalgia
diagnostic_criteria: Severe localized toothache, gingival swelling, percussion tenderness, fever, or pressure-change pain
autonomous_checklist: Inspect Amoxicillin/Clavulanate 875/125 mg blister pack for spaceflight API discoloration before dosing
Administer Amoxicillin/Clavulanate 875/125 mg PO q12h (or Azithromycin if PCN-allergic and QTc normal)
Manage pain with Acetaminophen 650 mg PO (or Ibuprofen 400 mg if no stone history) and place temporary dental filling if crown/filling lost
drug_lockouts: Amoxicillin/Clavulanate if PCN allergy
Ibuprofen if renal calculi history

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Skin & Soft Tissue Infection (Cellulitis / Abscess)
diagnostic_criteria: Expanding erythema, warmth, tenderness, induration, or purulent fluctuance
autonomous_checklist: Cleanse superficial abrasions and apply Bacitracin ointment
For purulent cellulitis / CA-MRSA: Doxycycline 100 mg PO BID (with full water flush) or TMP-SMX 800/160 mg PO BID
Perform incision and drainage (I&D) in contained field if fluctuant abscess present
drug_lockouts: Trimethoprim/SMX if ARS / BFO radiation risk or hyperkalemia
Doxycycline during high UV exposure (photosensitivity)

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Herpes Zoster (Shingles) / Latent Viral Reactivation
diagnostic_criteria: Painful unilateral dermatomal vesicular rash, prodromal burning/tingling
autonomous_checklist: Verify baseline renal function on i-STAT Chem8+ creatinine
Initiate Valacyclovir 1 g PO TID x 7 days within 72 hours of rash onset
Maintain high oral hydration to prevent acyclovir crystal nephropathy and cover lesions to prevent crew transmission
drug_lockouts: Unadjusted Valacyclovir in severe dehydration / renal impairment

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Cutaneous Fungal Dermatitis (Tinea / Candidiasis)
diagnostic_criteria: Pruritic annular scaly plaques or intertriginous macerated rash
autonomous_checklist: Inspect Clotrimazole 1% cream for emulsion phase separation if mission duration > 880 days
Apply Clotrimazole 1% cream BID; escalate to Fluconazole 150 mg PO for refractory/mucocutaneous cases
drug_lockouts: Hydrocortisone 1% cream (worsens fungal infection)
Fluconazole if elevated AST/ALT or QTc > 470 ms

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: EVA Musculoskeletal Strain / Suit Shoulder Injury
diagnostic_criteria: Localized shoulder, wrist, or lumbar strain following EVA or ARED resistive exercise without neurovascular deficit
autonomous_checklist: Confirm no history of renal calculi before offering Ibuprofen 400 mg PO q6h
Use Acetaminophen 650 mg PO if renal stones or dehydration present
Modify ARED loading and restrict EVA until range of motion recovers
drug_lockouts: Ibuprofen if renal calculi history or dehydration

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Blunt Trauma & Hemorrhage Control (eFAST Protocol)
diagnostic_criteria: High-energy impact or crush injury
Ultrasound-2 eFAST: Positive pericardial, pleural, or peritoneal free fluid
i-STAT CG4+: Rising lactate, metabolic acidosis
autonomous_checklist: Perform Ultrasound-2 eFAST exam and establish large-bore IV access (ISP)
Administer IV crystalloids and titrate Hydromorphone 1-2 mg IV (only if ppCO2 nominal)
Monitor continuous hemodynamics on Tempus Pro
drug_lockouts: Aspirin, Ibuprofen, Ketorolac, Apixaban, Enoxaparin, Clopidogrel (hemorrhage)
clinical_practice_guidelines.search_text: CPG-28 Blunt Trauma Hemorrhage Control Ultrasound-2 eFAST free fluid i-STAT CG4+ lactate Hydromorphone IV fluids.

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Acute Gastroenteritis / Infectious Diarrhea
diagnostic_criteria: Acute watery diarrhea, abdominal cramping, nausea
autonomous_checklist: Rule out Acute Radiation Syndrome (ARS) GI prodrome and dysentery (blood/high fever)
Initiate oral/IV rehydration and Ondansetron 4-8 mg ODT
Administer Loperamide 2 mg PO only if afebrile, non-bloody, and non-ARS
drug_lockouts: Loperamide if ARS GI syndrome, bloody stool, high fever, or suspected SBO

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Spaceflight Constipation / Bowel Dysmotility
diagnostic_criteria: Reduced bowel movement frequency, mild bloating without rebound tenderness or fever
autonomous_checklist: Rule out acute surgical abdomen / appendicitis / Small Bowel Obstruction (SBO)
Increase fluid intake and administer Bisacodyl 5-10 mg PO
drug_lockouts: Bisacodyl if acute surgical abdomen or SBO suspected

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Circadian Misalignment & Acute Insomnia
diagnostic_criteria: 90-minute orbital light/dark cycle disruption or slam-shift schedule
Sleep latency > 30 min or total sleep < 6 hours; sleep-quarter noise > 48 dBA (NC-40)
autonomous_checklist: Enforce acoustic limit <= 48 dBA (NC-40) and block blue light pre-sleep
Administer Melatonin 3 mg PO 30-60 min before target sleep
For refractory insomnia: Zaleplon 10 mg PO (short window) or Zolpidem 5 mg PO (>=6-8h protected window)
drug_lockouts: Zolpidem if EVA or critical alarm response required within 6-8 hours, or if ppCO2 elevated

clinical_practice_guidelines.title: Mission Fatigue & Cognitive Sustainment
diagnostic_criteria: Extended contingency shift, acute sleep deprivation, declining reaction time
autonomous_checklist: Verify absence of tachyarrhythmias on Tempus Pro and adequate hydration
Administer Caffeine 100-200 mg PO for short-term alertness or Modafinil 200 mg PO for extended contingency shifts
drug_lockouts: Tachyarrhythmias (Afib/SVT), severe dehydration, uncontrolled hypertension
